newsitem.title: USA: Dow seen up 50 to 80 points at open, Japan calms.
newsitem.headline: Dow seen up 50 to 80 points at open, Japan calms.

text.p: Dow industrials were expected to open between 50 and 80 points higher on Tuesday, driven by bargain hunting after yesterday's steep sell-off and reassured by Japanese government comments regarding Japan's holdings of U.S. government bonds.
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up eight points at 889.75 and the long bond rose 7/32 to yield 6.69 percent.

"The market could open up 50 to 80 points higher, though that's a guess because programs will kick in," Ron Doran, director of institutional trading at C.L. King and Associates, said. "A lot of yesterday's sell-off was not warranted."

U.S. stocks sank on Monday after Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, responding to a question following a speech at Columbia University in New York, was quoted as saying Japan in the past had been tempted to sell U.S. government bond holdings and boost its gold reserves but had not done so.
But Japan's Finance Ministry moved to calm markets, saying Hashimoto's "real intention" had been incorrectly reported.
A senior finance ministry said American government bonds were an essential investment tool in Japan's foreign reserves.
Charles White, managing director of Avatar Associates, also said he saw the Dow adding 50 to 70 points at the open.
